title: Hubris syndrome and the safeguards that keep a leader open to challenge — “good intentions alone are not enough”
summary: Batista is reading the book and takes up its discussion of hubris syndrome, the term Owen and Davidson proposed in 2009 for the overconfidence that follows long-held, unchecked power. His conclusion is that intentions are not a safeguard, and he lists three that are: someone assigned to question assumptions, a safe route to speak up, and a failure discussion before approval.
blockquote: My takeaway from Ries is that good intentions alone are not enough. Companies need safeguards that keep leaders open to challenge, especially when they have the authority to override everyone else.
